sections.title: Module 14: Understanding the differences
sections.body:
| Concept | Purpose |
|--------|--------|
| Logging | Record individual events |
| Tracing | Follow one request across components |
| Metrics | Measure system behavior numerically |
| Monitoring | Track metrics and trigger alerts |
| Observability | Understand internal behavior through telemetry |
| Evaluation | Measure response and retrieval quality |

steps.label: Query
steps.narration: The user query enters the system and may need rewriting before search.

steps.label: Transform
steps.narration: Query transformation expands, rewrites, or decomposes the question to improve recall.

steps.label: Search
steps.narration: Dense and/or keyword search return candidate passages.

steps.label: Fuse
steps.narration: Fusion methods such as RRF combine rankings from multiple retrievers into one list.

steps.label: Rerank
steps.narration: A cross-encoder or LLM reranker reorders candidates for higher precision context.

steps.label: Context
steps.narration: Final context is budgeted, ordered, and injected into the prompt for grounded generation.

### What should be captured in traces?

Capture request ID, trace ID, span ID, model name, model version, document IDs, retrieval strategy, similarity scores, token usage, latency, retry count, error category, estimated cost and evaluation scores.

Avoid storing sensitive documents, secrets and personal information in plaintext logs.

| Prometheus | Operational metrics |
| Grafana | Dashboards and alerts |
| Azure Application Insights | Azure application monitoring |
